sourceDate.text: 太祖為江南行中書省平章
太祖為江南行中書省平章
太祖為江南行中書省平章

units.zh: 李善長
units.en: Li Shanzhang
units.literal: Li Shanzhang

units.zh: 李善長，字百室，定遠人。
units.en: Li Shanzhang, whose style was Baishi, came from Dingyuan.
units.literal: Li Shanzhang, styled Baishi, was a native of Dingyuan.

units.zh: 少讀書有智計，習法家言，策事多中。
units.en: As a young man he read widely and showed shrewd judgment; versed in Legalist doctrine, his counsel on affairs proved sound again and again.
units.literal: In youth he studied and possessed resourcefulness; he practiced Legalist teachings, and in planning affairs he was often right.

units.zh: 太祖略地滁陽，善長迎謁。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor was expanding his hold around Chuyang on the Chu frontier, Shanzhang came forward to greet him.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor was seizing territory around Chuyang in Chu prefecture, Shanzhang went out to meet and pay his respects.

units.zh: 知其為里中長者，禮之，留掌書記。
units.en: Recognizing him as a leading man of the locality, the Emperor honored him, retained him, and appointed him to manage written records.
units.literal: Knowing him to be an elder of the district, the Emperor treated him with ceremony, kept him, and put him in charge of secretarial records.

units.zh: 嘗從容問曰：「四方戰鬥，何時定乎？」
units.en: On one occasion the Emperor asked him casually, "Fighting rages in every quarter—when will the realm be settled?"
units.literal: Once, speaking at ease, he asked: "Battles rage on every side—when will they end?"

units.zh: 對曰：「秦亂，漢高起布衣，豁達大度，知人善任，不嗜殺人，五載成帝業。
units.en: Shanzhang answered, "When the Qin order collapsed, Liu Bang rose from the ranks of commoners—open-handed, magnanimous, skilled at knowing men and putting them to use, sparing of bloodshed—and within five years he had won the empire.
units.literal: He replied: "When the Qin fell into chaos, Emperor Gaozu of Han rose from common cloth, was open and magnanimous, knew men and employed them well, did not delight in killing, and within five years accomplished the imperial enterprise.

units.zh: 今元綱既紊，天下土崩瓦解。
units.en: Today the Yuan statutes are in disarray and the empire is breaking apart.
units.literal: Now the Yuan dynasty's laws are already in disorder, and the realm is crumbling apart.

units.zh: 公濠產，距沛不遠。
units.en: Your Lordship is a son of the Huai country, and Pei lies not far away.
units.literal: Your Lordship was born in the Huai region, not far from Pei.

units.zh: 山川王氣，公當受之。
units.en: The mountains and rivers here breathe the air of kingship; you are the one destined to receive it.
units.literal: Mountains and rivers bear the aura of kingship—you ought to receive it.

units.zh: 法其所為，天下不足定也。」
units.en: Follow his example, and bringing the realm under your rule will not be difficult."
units.literal: Imitate what he did, and the realm will be no hard thing to settle."

units.zh: 太祖稱善。
units.en: The Founding Emperor approved his words.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor praised this as good.

units.zh: 從下滁州，為參謀，預機畫，主饋餉，甚見親信。
units.en: When Chuzhou was taken he served as adviser on the staff, shared in planning operations, and directed supply lines, winning deep trust.
units.literal: Following the capture of Chuzhou, he served as staff adviser, took part in strategic planning, and was put in charge of provisions; he was greatly trusted.

units.zh: 太祖威名日盛，諸將來歸者，善長察其材，言之太祖。
units.en: As the Founding Emperor's fame spread, every commander who came to join him was assessed by Shanzhang for ability and recommended to the throne.
units.literal: As the Founding Emperor's renown grew daily, when generals came to submit, Shanzhang sized up their talents and reported them to the Emperor.

units.zh: 復為太祖布款誠，使皆得自安。
units.en: He also spoke reassuringly on the Emperor's behalf so that each man might feel himself secure.
units.literal: Again he spread sincere goodwill on the Emperor's behalf, so that all might rest secure.

units.zh: 有以事力相齟齬者，委曲為調護。
units.en: When rivals quarreled over precedence or power, he smoothed matters with tact and shielded them from harm.
units.literal: When some clashed over strength of position, he tactfully mediated and protected them.

units.zh: 郭子興中流言，疑太祖，稍奪其兵柄。
units.en: Guo Zixing, hearing malicious talk, came to doubt the Founding Emperor and little by little withdrew his command.
units.literal: Guo Zixing, swayed by slander, grew suspicious of the Founding Emperor and gradually stripped him of military authority.

units.zh: 又欲奪善長自輔，善長固謝弗往。
units.en: Guo also tried to draw Shanzhang away to serve at his side, but Shanzhang steadfastly refused.
units.literal: He also wished to take Shanzhang away to assist himself; Shanzhang firmly declined and would not go.

units.zh: 太祖深倚之。
units.en: The Founding Emperor leaned on him all the more.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor relied on him deeply.

units.zh: 太祖軍和陽，自將擊雞籠山寨，少留兵佐善長居守。
units.en: While the army was encamped at Heyang, the Founding Emperor led the assault on Jilong Mountain himself, leaving Shanzhang behind with a modest garrison.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor's army was at Heyang, he personally led an attack on Jilong Mountain stockade, leaving only a small force with Shanzhang to hold the camp.

units.zh: 元將諜知來襲，設伏敗之，太祖以為能。
units.en: Yuan scouts discovered the weakness and struck; Shanzhang laid an ambush and routed them, and the Founding Emperor judged him capable.
units.literal: A Yuan general learned by espionage and came to raid; Shanzhang set an ambush and defeated him, and the Founding Emperor considered him capable.

units.zh: 太祖得巢湖水師，善長力贊渡江。
units.en: After the Chaohu flotilla came over, Shanzhang pressed hard for a crossing of the Yangzi.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor obtained the Chaohu water force, Shanzhang strongly urged crossing the Yangzi.

units.zh: 既拔採石，趨太平，善長預書榜禁戢士卒。
units.en: Once Caishi fell they hurried toward Taiping; Shanzhang had already drafted a proclamation restraining the soldiers.
units.literal: After taking Caishi they pressed on to Taiping; Shanzhang beforehand drafted a placard forbidding the troops.

units.zh: 城下，即揭之通衢，肅然無敢犯者。
units.en: As soon as the city surrendered the notice went up in the public ways, and discipline held so firmly that no one dared transgress.
units.literal: When the city fell, it was at once posted in the main thoroughfares, and all stood in awe—none dared violate it.

units.zh: 太祖為太平興國翼大元帥，以為帥府都事。
units.en: Made Grand Marshal of the Pacifying State and Flourishing Wings, the Founding Emperor named Shanzhang director of the marshal's headquarters.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor became Grand Marshal of the Pacifying State and Flourishing Wings, and appointed Shanzhang director of the marshal's headquarters.

units.zh: 從克集慶。
units.en: He took part in the reduction of Jiqing.
units.literal: He followed in the capture of Jiqing.

units.zh: 將取鎮江，太祖慮諸將不戢下，乃佯怒欲置諸法，善長力救得解。
units.en: Before the assault on Zhenjiang the Founding Emperor worried that his commanders would not keep their men in hand; he pretended to rage and threatened legal punishment, until Shanzhang's earnest intercession won them pardon.
units.literal: About to take Zhenjiang, the Founding Emperor feared the generals would not restrain their men below them; he therefore feigned anger and wished to punish them by law, but Shanzhang strenuously pleaded and secured their release.

units.zh: 鎮江下，民不知有兵。
units.en: Zhenjiang submitted so quietly that the populace hardly knew troops had been there.
units.literal: When Zhenjiang fell, the people scarcely knew an army had passed.

units.zh: 太祖為江南行中書省平章，以為參議。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor became Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, Shanzhang was appointed deliberator.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor became Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, Shanzhang was made a deliberator.

units.zh: 時宋思顏、李夢庚、郭景祥等俱為省僚，而軍機進退，賞罰章程，多決於善長。
units.en: Song Siyan, Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, and others served beside him in the province, but questions of campaign, promotion, reward, and punishment fell largely to Shanzhang.
units.literal: At the time Song Siyan, Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, and others were all provincial colleagues, yet military decisions, advances and retreats, and rules of reward and punishment were largely settled by Shanzhang.

units.zh: 改樞密院為大都督府，命兼領府司馬，進行省參知政事。
units.en: The Bureau of Military Affairs became the Office of the Grand Marshal; Shanzhang was ordered to serve concurrently as its secretary and was advanced to Vice Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat.
units.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs was changed into the Office of the Grand Marshal; he was ordered to head the office concurrently as marshal's secretary, and was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat.

units.zh: 太祖為吳王，拜右相國。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor took the title Prince of Wu, Shanzhang was named Right Chancellor of State.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor became Prince of Wu, Shanzhang was appointed Right Chancellor of State.

units.zh: 善長明習故事，裁決如流，又嫻於辭命。
units.en: Well versed in precedent, he decided cases with fluent ease and was equally adept at drafting imperial communications.
units.literal: Shanzhang was clear in precedent and custom; his judgments flowed like water, and he was moreover skilled in drafting commands.

units.zh: 太祖有所招納，輒令為書。
units.en: Whenever the Founding Emperor sought to win someone over, he had Shanzhang write the message.
units.literal: Whenever the Founding Emperor wished to win someone over, he would order Shanzhang to compose the letter.

units.zh: 前後自將征討，皆命居守，將吏帖服，居民安堵，轉調兵餉無乏。
units.en: On every campaign the Emperor left him to hold the rear: subordinates obeyed, townsfolk lived undisturbed, and troops and grain moved without fail.
units.literal: Before and after, whenever the Emperor led campaigns in person, he always ordered Shanzhang to remain and guard the base; officers and clerks submitted to him, the people lived in peace, and the transfer of troops and grain never fell short.

units.zh: 嘗請榷兩淮鹽，立茶法，皆斟酌元制，去其弊政。
units.en: He proposed monopolizing salt in the two Huai circuits and instituting tea laws, each measure adapting Yuan practice while stripping away its abuses.
units.literal: He once requested a monopoly on salt in the two Huai circuits and the establishment of tea regulations, all weighing the Yuan system and removing its harmful policies.

units.zh: 既復製錢法，開鐵冶，定魚稅，國用益饒，而民不困。
units.en: Once coinage, ironworks, and the fish levy were reordered, the treasury grew ample yet the common people did not suffer.
units.literal: After restoring the coinage law, opening iron works, and fixing the fish tax, state revenue grew richer while the people were not distressed.

units.zh: 吳元年九月論平吳功，封善長宣國公。
units.en: In the ninth month of Wu year one, when rewards for pacifying Wu were apportioned, Shanzhang was enfeoffed Duke of Xuan.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Wu, when the merit of pacifying Wu was discussed, Shanzhang was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuan.

units.zh: 改官制，尚左，以為左相國。
units.en: When offices were reorganized to honor the left, he became Left Chancellor of State.
units.literal: When the official system was revised and the left was honored, he was made Left Chancellor of State.

units.zh: 太祖初渡江，頗用重典，一日，謂善長：「法有連坐三條，不已甚乎？」
units.en: In his early days south of the river the Founding Emperor relied on harsh law; one day he told Shanzhang, "The code provides three kinds of kin punishment for a single crime—is that not too severe?"
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor first crossed the Yangzi he used severe statutes heavily; one day he said to Shanzhang: "The law has three articles of collective punishment—is that not excessive?"

units.zh: 善長因請自大逆而外皆除之，遂命與中丞劉基等裁定律令，頒示中外。
units.en: Shanzhang asked that every offense save grand treason be struck from collective punishment; the Emperor then ordered him, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Ji, and others to revise the code and publish it throughout the realm.
units.literal: Shanzhang thereupon requested that all but grand treason be abolished, and the Emperor then ordered him together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Ji and others to trim the laws and statutes and promulgate them within and without.

units.zh: 太祖即帝位，追帝祖考及冊立後妃太子諸王，皆以善長充大禮使。
units.en: At his accession, whenever the throne honored imperial ancestors or invested empress, heir, and princes, Shanzhang served as chief ritual commissioner.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the imperial throne, in posthumously honoring his forebears and in investing the empress, the heir apparent, and the princes, Shanzhang was always appointed chief ritual commissioner.

units.zh: 置東宮官屬，以善長兼太子少師，授銀青榮祿大夫、上柱國，錄軍國重事，餘如故。
units.en: When the heir's household was staffed, Shanzhang became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, received Silver-Green Glory Grandee and Upper Pillar of State, was charged to record weighty civil and military affairs, and otherwise kept his posts.
units.literal: When the Eastern Palace staff was established, Shanzhang was additionally made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, granted Silver-Green Glory Grandee and Upper Pillar of State, recorded weighty affairs of army and state, and the rest of his duties remained as before.

units.zh: 已，帥禮官定郊社宗廟禮。
units.en: He then directed the ritual officers in setting the ceremonies for suburban sacrifice, altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temples.
units.literal: Thereafter he led the ritual officials in fixing the rites of suburban sacrifice, altars of soil and grain, and ancestral temples.

units.zh: 帝幸汴梁，善長留守，一切聽便宜行事。
units.en: While the Emperor was at Bianliang, Shanzhang stayed behind with full authority to act as he saw fit.
units.literal: When the Emperor visited Bianliang, Shanzhang remained on guard and was empowered to act entirely at his discretion.

units.zh: 尋奏定六部官制，議官民喪服及朝賀東宮儀。
units.en: He soon submitted plans for the Six Ministries, rules for mourning dress among officials and commoners, and ceremonies for court audience and homage to the heir.
units.literal: Soon he memorialized to fix the official system of the Six Ministries, and deliberated mourning dress for officials and commoners and the rites of court audience and homage to the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 奉命監修《元史》，編《祖訓錄》、《大明集禮》諸書。
units.en: Commissioned to oversee the 《History of the Yuan》, he also helped compile the 《Records of Ancestral Instruction》 and the 《Collected Rites of the Great Ming》.
units.literal: Ordered to supervise compilation of the 《History of the Yuan》, he also edited such works as 《Records of Ancestral Instruction》 and 《Collected Rites of the Great Ming》.

units.zh: 定天下岳瀆神祗封號，封建諸王，爵賞功臣，事無巨細，悉委善長與諸儒臣謀議行之。
units.en: Titles for the empire's sacred mountains and rivers, investiture of princes, ennoblement of meritorious servants—matters great and small were referred to Shanzhang and the scholar-officials for deliberation and execution.
units.literal: Fixing the titles of the sacred peaks and rivers of the realm, enfeoffing the princes, granting ranks and rewards to meritorious ministers—whether great or small, all were entrusted to Shanzhang and the Confucian officials to deliberate and carry out.

units.zh: 洪武三年大封功臣。
units.en: In Hongwu year three came the great enfeoffment of founding ministers.
units.literal: In the third year of Hongwu there was a great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers.

units.zh: 帝謂：「善長雖無汗馬勞，然事朕久，給軍食，功甚大，宜進封大國。」
units.en: The Emperor said, "Shanzhang never rode in the van, yet he has served Us long, fed the armies, and his service is surpassing; he deserves enfeoffment as duke of a great state."
units.literal: The Emperor said: "Although Shanzhang has no merit of sweat and horse, yet he has served Us long, supplied the army's food, and his merit is very great; he ought to be advanced to a great state."

units.zh: 乃授開國輔運推誠守正文臣、特進光祿大夫、左柱國、太師、中書左丞相，封韓國公，歲祿四千石，子孫世襲。
units.en: He received the titles Founding Assistant Minister Upholding Culture, specially advanced Glory Grandee of the First Rank, Left Pillar of State, Grand Preceptor, and Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed Duke of Han with four thousand piculs a year and hereditary succession.
units.literal: He was thereupon granted Founding Assistant Minister Upholding Culture, specially advanced Glory Grandee of the First Rank, Left Pillar of State, Grand Preceptor, Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, enfeoffed Duke of Han with an annual stipend of four thousand piculs, his descendants to inherit in perpetuity.

units.zh: 予鐵券，免二死，子免一死。
units.en: An iron certificate granted him two reprieves from capital punishment and his son one.
units.literal: He was given an iron certificate granting exemption from death twice, and his son exemption once.

units.zh: 時封公者，徐達、常遇春子茂、李文忠、馮勝、鄧愈及善長六人。
units.en: Six men received ducal rank: Xu Da, Mao son of Chang Yuchun, Li Wenzhong, Feng Sheng, Deng Yu, and Shanzhang.
units.literal: At that time those enfeoffed as dukes were six: Xu Da, Chang Yuchun's son Mao, Li Wenzhong, Feng Sheng, Deng Yu, and Shanzhang.

units.zh: 而善長位第一，制詞比之蕭何，褒稱甚至。
units.en: Shanzhang nevertheless ranked first; the enfeoffment text likened him to Xiao He, and the praise was lavish.
units.literal: Yet Shanzhang stood first in rank; the patent of enfeoffment compared him to Xiao He, and the praise was extreme.

units.zh: 善長外寬和，內多忮刻。
units.en: Outwardly he was gentle and accommodating; inwardly he was quick to resent.
units.literal: Outwardly Shanzhang was mild and harmonious, inwardly he was much given to envy.

units.zh: 參議李飲冰、楊希聖，稍侵善長權，即按其罪奏黜之。
units.en: When deliberators Li Yinbing and Yang Xisheng encroached on his authority, he found cause against them and had them cashiered.
units.literal: Deliberators Li Yinbing and Yang Xisheng, who slightly encroached on Shanzhang's power, he at once investigated for crimes and memorialized to dismiss them.

units.zh: 與中丞劉基爭法而訽。
units.en: He clashed with Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Ji over legal policy and abused him.
units.literal: He quarreled with Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Ji over the law and reviled him.

units.zh: 基不自安，請告歸。
units.en: Liu Ji, ill at ease, asked permission to withdraw.
units.literal: Ji could not feel secure and requested leave to retire.

units.zh: 太祖所任張昶、楊憲、汪廣洋、胡惟庸皆獲罪，善長事寄如故。
units.en: Zhang Chang, Yang Xian, Wang Guangyang, and Hu Weiyong, whom the throne had raised, all fell for crime, yet Shanzhang's trust held.
units.literal: Zhang Chang, Yang Xian, Wang Guangyang, and Hu Weiyong, whom the Founding Emperor appointed, all fell into crime, yet Shanzhang's commission remained as before.

units.zh: 貴富極，意稍驕，帝始微厭之。
units.en: Flush with wealth and rank, he grew somewhat arrogant, and the Emperor's favor cooled.
units.literal: At the height of wealth and honor his mind grew somewhat proud, and the Emperor began to dislike him slightly.

units.zh: 四年以疾致仕，賜臨濠地若干頃，置守塚戶百五十，給佃戶千五百家，儀仗士二十家。
units.en: In year four he retired ill; the throne granted him land near Linhao, one hundred fifty grave-keeper households, fifteen hundred tenant families, and twenty ceremonial guards.
units.literal: In the fourth year, on grounds of illness he retired from office; he was granted several qing of land at Linhao, one hundred fifty grave-keeper households, fifteen hundred tenant households, and twenty ceremonial guard households.

units.zh: 逾年，病癒，命董建臨濠宮殿。
units.en: A year later, recovered, he was ordered to oversee the palace works at Linhao.
units.literal: After more than a year his illness healed, and he was ordered to supervise construction of the palace at Linhao.

units.zh: 徙江南富民十四萬田濠州，以善長經理之，留濠者數年。
units.en: One hundred forty thousand prosperous Jiangnan households were relocated to Hao with their lands for Shanzhang to manage, and he stayed there several years.
units.literal: One hundred forty thousand wealthy families of Jiangnan were moved to Hao prefecture with their fields for Shanzhang to administer; he remained at Hao several years.

units.zh: 七年擢善長弟存義為太僕丞，存義子伸、佑皆為群牧所官。
units.en: In year seven his brother Cunyi became Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, and Cunyi's sons Shen and You received posts in the Pasturage Office.
units.literal: In the seventh year his younger brother Cunyi was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud; Cunyi's sons Shen and You were all made officers of the Pasturage Office.

units.zh: 九年以臨安公主歸其子祺，拜駙馬都尉。
units.en: In year nine the Princess of Lin'an married his son Qi, who was named Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
units.literal: In the ninth year the Princess of Lin'an was married to his son Qi, who was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.

units.zh: 初定婚禮，公主修婦道甚肅。
units.en: As wedding protocol was first established, the princess conducted herself as a daughter-in-law with strict propriety.
units.literal: When the marriage rites were first fixed, the princess observed a wife's conduct with great propriety.

units.zh: 光寵赫奕，時人豔之。
units.en: Honor and splendor shone on the house, and contemporaries looked on with envy.
units.literal: Glory and favor blazed brilliantly, and men of the time envied them.

units.zh: 祺尚主後一月，御史大夫汪廣洋、陳寧疏言：「善長狎寵自恣，陛下病不視朝幾及旬，不問候。
units.en: A month after Qi's marriage, Censor-in-Chief Wang Guangyang and Chen Ning reported, "Shanzhang, emboldened by favor, had failed to attend the Emperor during a ten-day illness.
units.literal: One month after Qi married the princess, Censor-in-Chief Wang Guangyang and Chen Ning memorialized: "Shanzhang, taking favor for license, acts as he pleases; when Your Majesty was ill and did not hold court for nearly ten days, he did not inquire after you.

units.zh: 駙馬都尉祺六日不朝，宣至殿前，又不引罪，大不敬。」
units.en: Qi himself absented court for six days and, when summoned, refused to confess fault—an act of grave disrespect."
units.literal: The Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law Qi did not attend court for six days; summoned to the hall, he again did not acknowledge guilt—great disrespect.

units.zh: 坐削歲祿千八百石。
units.en: For this his annual stipend was cut by eighteen hundred piculs.
units.literal: On this charge his annual stipend was reduced by eighteen hundred piculs.

units.zh: 尋命與曹國公李文忠總中書省大都督府御史台，同議軍國大事，督圜丘工。
units.en: He was soon ordered with Duke of Cao Li Wenzhong to direct the Secretariat, Grand Marshal's Office, and Censorate, deliberate state affairs, and supervise the Round Mound altar.
units.literal: Soon he was ordered together with Duke of Cao Li Wenzhong to oversee the Secretariat, the Office of the Grand Marshal, and the Censorate, jointly to deliberate great affairs of army and state and supervise work on the Round Mound.

units.zh: 丞相胡惟庸初為甯國知縣，以善長薦，擢太常少卿，後為丞相，因相往來。
units.en: Hu Weiyong had been magistrate of Ningguo; Shanzhang recommended him, he rose to Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices and then chancellor, and the two kept up ties.
units.literal: Chancellor Hu Weiyong had first been magistrate of Ningguo; through Shanzhang's recommendation he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, later became chancellor, and therefore maintained mutual dealings.

units.zh: 而善長弟存義子佑，惟庸從女婿也。
units.en: Shanzhang's nephew You, son of his brother Cunyi, was married to Hu Weiyong's daughter.
units.literal: Yet Shanzhang's younger brother Cunyi's son You was Hu Weiyong's son-in-law by marriage.

units.zh: 十三年，惟庸謀反伏誅，坐党死者甚眾，善長如故。
units.en: In year thirteen Hu Weiyong's treason was uncovered and he was executed; many partisans perished, but Shanzhang was untouched.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year Hu Weiyong's plot to rebel was exposed and he was executed; many died as partisans, yet Shanzhang remained as before.

units.zh: 御史台缺中丞，以善長理台事，數有所建白。
units.en: With no vice censor-in-chief in the Censorate, Shanzhang directed its business and several times submitted recommendations.
units.literal: The Censorate lacked a vice censor-in-chief; Shanzhang was put in charge of censorial affairs and several times offered proposals.

units.zh: 十八年，有人告存義父子實惟庸黨者，詔免死，安置崇明。
units.en: In year eighteen informers named Cunyi and his son as Hu's partisans; an edict spared their lives and exiled them to Chongming.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year someone reported that Cunyi father and son were in truth partisans of Hu Weiyong; an edict spared their lives and settled them at Chongming.

units.zh: 善長不謝，帝銜之。
units.en: Shanzhang offered no thanks, and the Emperor took offense.
units.literal: Shanzhang did not thank the Emperor, and the Emperor harbored resentment.

units.zh: 又五年，善長年已七十有七，耄不檢下。
units.en: Five years later, aged seventy-seven, he no longer kept his household in check.
units.literal: After another five years Shanzhang was already seventy-seven; in senility he did not restrain his household.

units.zh: 嘗欲營第，從信國公湯和假衛卒三百人，和密以聞。
units.en: When he sought to build a residence he borrowed three hundred guards from Duke of Trust Tang He, who quietly informed the throne.
units.literal: Once wishing to build a mansion, he borrowed three hundred guard soldiers from Duke of Trust Tang He; He secretly reported it.

units.zh: 四月，京民坐罪應徙邊者，善長數請免其私親丁斌等。
units.en: In the fourth month, as condemned capital residents were sent to the border, Shanzhang repeatedly pleaded for his clients Ding Bin and others.
units.literal: In the fourth month, when capital residents guilty of crimes were to be exiled to the frontier, Shanzhang repeatedly asked exemption for his private connections Ding Bin and others.

units.zh: 帝怒按斌，斌故給事惟庸家，因言存義等往時交通惟庸狀。
units.en: The Emperor had Bin interrogated; Bin, once a servant in Hu's house, described Cunyi's earlier contacts with Hu.
units.literal: The Emperor angrily investigated Bin; Bin had formerly served in Hu Weiyong's household and therefore spoke of how Cunyi and others in former times had dealings with Hu Weiyong.

units.zh: 命逮存義父子鞫之，詞連善長，云：「惟庸有反謀，使存義陰說善長。
units.en: Cunyi and his son were arrested; their testimony touched Shanzhang: "Hu had plotted rebellion and sent Cunyi to win him over.
units.literal: He ordered Cunyi father and son seized and examined; their testimony implicated Shanzhang, saying: "Hu Weiyong had a plot to rebel and had Cunyi secretly persuade Shanzhang.

units.zh: 善長驚叱曰：『爾言何為者！
units.en: Shanzhang cried out in alarm, 'What nonsense is this!
units.literal: Shanzhang in alarm rebuked him: "What words are these you speak!"

units.zh: 審爾，九族皆滅！』
units.en: If that were true, nine degrees of kin would perish!'
units.literal: If it is truly so, nine degrees of kin will all be destroyed!

units.zh: 已，又使善長故人楊文裕說之云：『事成當以淮西地封為王。』
units.en: Later Hu sent Shanzhang's old friend Yang Wenyu, promising, 'If the plot succeeded he would be made king of the Huai-west lands.'
units.literal: Afterward he again had Shanzhang's old acquaintance Yang Wenyu persuade him, saying: "When the affair succeeds you will be enfeoffed king over the land west of the Huai.

units.zh: 善長驚不許，然頗心動。
units.en: Shanzhang refused in alarm, yet his heart wavered.
units.literal: Shanzhang in alarm did not consent, yet his heart was somewhat moved.

units.zh: 惟庸乃自往說善長，猶不許。
units.en: Hu Weiyong came in person to persuade him, and still he would not agree.
units.literal: Hu Weiyong then went in person to persuade Shanzhang, and he still did not consent.

units.zh: 居久之，惟庸復遣存義進說，善長歎曰：『吾老矣。
units.en: Long afterward Hu sent Cunyi again; Shanzhang sighed, 'I am old.
units.literal: After a long while Hu Weiyong again sent Cunyi to advance the persuasion; Shanzhang sighed: "I am old."

units.zh: 吾死，汝等自為之！』」
units.en: When I am gone, do as you please among yourselves!'"
units.literal: When I die, do as you will yourselves!"

units.zh: 或又告善長云：「將軍藍玉出塞，至捕魚兒海，獲惟庸通沙漠使者封績，善長匿不以聞。」
units.en: Another informer said to Shanzhang, "General Lan Yu, campaigning beyond the frontier, had seized Hu's messenger Feng Ji at Buyur Lake, and Shanzhang had hidden the fact without reporting it."
units.literal: Or again someone reported to Shanzhang: "General Lan Yu, going beyond the pass, reached Buyur Lake and captured Hu Weiyong's envoy to the desert, Feng Ji; Shanzhang concealed it and did not report."

units.zh: 於是御史交章劾善長。
units.en: Censors then impeached him in a flood of memorials.
units.literal: Thereupon censors submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Shanzhang.

units.zh: 而善長奴盧仲謙等，亦告善長與惟庸通賂遺，交私語。
units.en: Slaves such as Lu Zhongqian also testified to bribes and secret talk between Shanzhang and Hu.
units.literal: Moreover Shanzhang's slave Lu Zhongqian and others also reported that Shanzhang and Hu Weiyong exchanged bribes and gifts and spoke in private.

units.zh: 獄具，謂善長元勳國戚，知逆謀不發舉，狐疑觀望懷兩端，大逆不道。
units.en: The verdict held that Shanzhang, founding minister and imperial kin, knowing of treason yet failing to expose it and hedging between sides, had committed grand treason.
units.literal: When the case was complete, it was held that Shanzhang, a founding minister and imperial kin, knowing of the plot did not report it, wavered in doubt and looked to both sides—grand treason.

units.zh: 會有言星變，其占當移大臣。
units.en: A celestial anomaly was reported; its omen required the removal of a great minister.
units.literal: It happened that someone spoke of a change in the stars; the omen said a great minister must be removed.

units.zh: 遂並其妻女弟侄家口七十余人誅之。
units.en: His wife, children, brothers, nephews, and more than seventy dependents were executed together.
units.literal: Thereupon his wife, daughters, younger brothers, nephews, and household—more than seventy persons—were all executed.

units.zh: 而吉安侯陸仲亨、延安侯唐勝宗、平涼侯費聚、南雄侯趙庸、滎陽侯鄭遇春、宜春侯黃彬、河南侯陸聚等，皆同時坐惟庸黨死，而已故營陽侯楊璟、濟甯侯顧時等追坐者又若干人。
units.en: Marquis Lu Zhongheng of Ji'an, Tang Shengzong of Yan'an, Fei Ju of Pingliang, Zhao Yong of Nanxiong, Zheng Yuchun of Xingyang, Huang Bin of Yichun, Lu Ju of Henan, and others died as Hu's partisans; deceased Marquis Yang Jing of Yingyang, Gu Shi of Jining, and more were condemned posthumously.
units.literal: Marquis Lu Zhongheng of Ji'an, Marquis Tang Shengzong of Yan'an, Marquis Fei Ju of Pingliang, Marquis Zhao Yong of Nanxiong, Marquis Zheng Yuchun of Xingyang, Marquis Huang Bin of Yichun, Marquis Lu Ju of Henan, and others all died at the same time as partisans of Hu Weiyong, while the deceased Marquis Yang Jing of Yingyang, Marquis Gu Shi of Jining, and others were posthumously implicated—again several men.

units.zh: 帝手詔條列其罪，傅著獄辭，為《昭示奸黨三錄》，佈告天下。
units.en: The Emperor penned an edict itemizing their crimes, attached it to the trial record, and published the 《Three Records Exposing the Traitorous Party》 throughout the empire.
units.literal: The Emperor in his own hand drafted an edict listing their crimes, appended it to the prison record, and made the 《Three Records Exposing the Traitorous Party》 to announce to the realm.

units.zh: 善長子祺與主徙江浦，久之卒。
units.en: Shanzhang's son Qi and the princess were exiled to Jiangpu; years later he died.
units.literal: Shanzhang's son Qi and the princess were banished to Jiangpu; after a long while he died.

units.zh: 祺子芳、茂，以公主恩得不坐。
units.en: Qi's sons Fang and Mao, by the princess's favor, escaped punishment.
units.literal: Qi's sons Fang and Mao, through the princess's grace, were not punished.

units.zh: 芳為留守中衛指揮，茂為旗手衛鎮撫，罷世襲。
units.en: Fang became commander of the Rear Guard, Mao registrar of the Banner Handlers; hereditary privilege was withdrawn.
units.literal: Fang became commander of the Rear Guard Garrison, Mao registrar of the Banner Handlers—hereditary succession was abolished.

units.zh: 善長死之明年，虞部郎中王國用上言：「善長與陛下同心，出萬死以取天下，勳臣第一，生封公，死封王，男尚公主，親戚拜官，人臣之分極矣。
units.en: In the year after Shanzhang died, Wang Guoyong, director in the Yu Bureau, submitted a memorial: "Shanzhang stood with Your Majesty in one purpose, risked death again and again to win the empire, and stood first among the founding ministers—duke in life, king in death, a son married to a princess, kinsmen raised to office. No subject could ask for more.
units.literal: The year after Shanzhang's death, Director Wang Guoyong of the Yu Bureau memorialized: "Shanzhang was of one mind with Your Majesty, braved myriad deaths to win the realm, ranked first among meritorious ministers, enfeoffed duke in life and king in death, his son married the princess, his kin granted office—the utmost a subject may receive.

units.zh: 藉令欲自圖不軌，尚未可知，而今謂其欲佐胡惟庸者，則大謬不然。
units.en: Even if one imagined he might plot on his own account, that would still be doubtful; to claim he meant to aid Hu Weiyong is simply wrong.
units.literal: Even if one supposed he wished to plot rebellion for himself, that would still be uncertain; but to say he wished to assist Hu Weiyong is a great error and not so.

units.zh: 人情愛其子，必甚于兄弟之子，安享萬全之富貴者，必不僥倖萬一之富貴。
units.en: Men love their own sons more than their brothers' sons; those who already enjoy secure and complete prosperity do not stake everything on a one-in-ten-thousand chance at more.
units.literal: In human feeling one loves one's own son more than a brother's son; one who enjoys wealth and honor in complete security will not gamble on wealth and honor that are one in ten thousand.

units.zh: 善長與惟庸，猶子之親耳，于陛下則親子女也。
units.en: Shanzhang's tie to Hu Weiyong was no closer than that of sons-in-law; toward Your Majesty he was bound by a daughter of the imperial house.
units.literal: Between Shanzhang and Hu Weiyong it was only the closeness of a brother's son; toward Your Majesty he was bound by the kinship of sons and daughters.

units.zh: 使善長佐惟庸成，不過勳臣第一而已矣，太師國公封王而已矣，尚主納妃而已矣，寧復有加於今日？
units.en: Had Shanzhang helped Hu Weiyong succeed, he would still be only first among ministers, Grand Preceptor, duke, king, imperial marriage—nothing beyond what he already possessed?
units.literal: If Shanzhang had assisted Hu Weiyong to success, he would be no more than first among meritorious ministers, Grand Preceptor and Duke of State enfeoffed as king, princess married and consort taken—how could there be increase beyond today?

units.zh: 且善長豈不知天下之不可幸取。
units.en: Surely Shanzhang knew the realm could not be seized by chance.
units.literal: Moreover, would Shanzhang not know that the realm cannot be seized by luck.

units.zh: 當元之季，欲為此者何限，莫不身為齏粉，覆宗絕祀，能保首領者幾何人哉？
units.en: In the Yuan's last days countless men tried such schemes; nearly all were ground to dust, their lines extinguished—how many kept their heads?
units.literal: At the end of the Yuan, how many wished to do this? None failed to become flesh paste, with clan extinguished and sacrifices cut off—how many could keep their heads?

units.zh: 善長胡乃身見之，而以衰倦之年身蹈之也。
units.en: Why would Shanzhang, who had seen this with his own eyes, in his weary old age walk into it himself.
units.literal: Why should Shanzhang, having seen this with his own body, in declining years tread it with his own person.

units.zh: 凡為此者，必有深仇激變，大不得已，父子之間或至相挾以求脫禍。
units.en: Men who do such things act under deadly grievance or dire compulsion; sometimes father and son even hold each other hostage to escape ruin.
units.literal: All who do this must have deep enmity and sudden change, great inability to do otherwise; between father and son they may even threaten one another to escape disaster.

units.zh: 今善長之子祺備陛下骨肉親，無纖芥嫌，何苦而忽為此。
units.en: Shanzhang's son Qi is Your Majesty's own kin by marriage, without the smallest quarrel—what reason would drive him to such a deed.
units.literal: Now Shanzhang's son Qi stands as Your Majesty's own flesh and blood in kinship, without the slightest grudge—why should he suddenly do this.

units.zh: 若謂天象告變，大臣當災，殺之以應天象，則尤不可。
units.en: If the argument is that a celestial omen demands a minister's death and he was killed to satisfy heaven, that is worse still.
units.literal: If one says the heavens' signs foretell change and a great minister must suffer disaster, and kills him to answer the sign, that is even more impossible.

units.zh: 臣恐天下聞之，謂功如善長且如此，四方因之解體也。
units.en: I fear the empire will hear that even a servant like Shanzhang came to this end, and the regions will lose heart.
units.literal: Your servant fears that when the realm hears of it, they will say that even merit like Shanzhang ends thus, and the four quarters will for that reason fall apart.

units.zh: 今善長已死，言之無益，所願陛下作戒將來耳。」
units.en: Shanzhang is dead and words cannot help him; I ask only that Your Majesty guard against such acts hereafter."
units.literal: Now Shanzhang is already dead; to speak is without benefit; what is wished is only that Your Majesty take warning for the future."

units.zh: 太祖得書，竟亦不罪也。
units.en: The Founding Emperor received the memorial and in the end did not punish him.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the memorial, in the end he did not punish him either.

units.zh: 汪廣洋
units.en: Wang Guangyang
units.literal: Wang Guangyang

units.zh: 汪廣洋，字朝宗，高郵人，流寓太平。
units.en: Wang Guangyang, whose style was Chaozong, came from Gaoyou and had settled in Taiping.
units.literal: Wang Guangyang, styled Chaozong, was a native of Gaoyou and sojourned in Taiping.

units.zh: 太祖渡江，召為元帥府令史，江南行省提控。
units.en: After the Founding Emperor crossed the Yangzi he was called to serve as clerk of the marshal's headquarters and controller of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor crossed the Yangzi, he was summoned as clerk of the Marshal's Headquarters and Controller of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.

units.zh: 置正軍都諫司，擢諫官，遷行省都事，累進中書右司郎中。
units.en: When the Direct Army Remonstrance Office was set up he became a remonstrance officer, then director of the branch secretariat, rising eventually to director of the Secretariat's right department.
units.literal: When the Direct Army Remonstrance Office was established, he was promoted remonstrance officer, transferred to director of the Branch Secretariat, and advanced step by step to Director of the Right Department of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 尋知驍騎衛事，參常遇春軍務。
units.en: He soon oversaw the Valiant Cavalry Guard and shared in Chang Yuchun's campaigns.
units.literal: Soon he was put in charge of the Valiant Cavalry Guard and took part in Chang Yuchun's military affairs.

units.zh: 下贛州，遂居守，拜江西參政。
units.en: After Ganzhou was taken he stayed as garrison commander and was named Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.
units.literal: When Ganzhou fell he remained to guard it and was appointed Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.

units.zh: 洪武元年，山東平，以廣洋廉明持重，命理行省，撫納新附，民甚安之。
units.en: In Hongwu year one, with Shandong pacified, his integrity and steadiness won him charge of the branch secretariat to settle new subjects; the people lived at ease.
units.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, when Shandong was pacified, because Guangyang was incorrupt, clear, and steady, he was ordered to administer the Branch Secretariat, comforting and accepting the newly submitted; the people were very much at peace.

units.zh: 是年召入為中書省參政。
units.en: That same year he was recalled to serve as Vice Commissioner of the Secretariat.
units.literal: That year he was summoned in as Vice Commissioner of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 明年出參政陝西。
units.en: The following year he was sent as Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi.
units.literal: The next year he went out as Vice Commissioner in Shaanxi.

units.zh: 三年，李善長病，中書無官，召廣洋為左丞。
units.en: In year three, when Li Shanzhang fell ill and the Secretariat stood vacant, Guangyang was summoned as Left Vice Director.
units.literal: In the third year Li Shanzhang fell ill; the Secretariat had no officer, and Guangyang was summoned as Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 時右丞楊憲專決事。
units.en: Right Vice Director Yang Xian then monopolized affairs.
units.literal: At the time Right Vice Director Yang Xian monopolized decisions.

units.zh: 廣洋依違之，猶為所忌，嗾御史劾廣洋奉母無狀。
units.en: Guangyang temporized and was still resented; Yang Xian set censors to accuse him of failing in filial duty toward his mother.
units.literal: Guangyang wavered in compliance and was still envied by him; he instigated censors to impeach Guangyang for misconduct in serving his mother.

units.zh: 帝切責，放還鄉。
units.en: The Emperor rebuked him sharply and sent him home.
units.literal: The Emperor sternly rebuked him and sent him back to his home district.

units.zh: 憲再奏，徙海南。
units.en: Yang Xian memorialized again and he was exiled to Hainan.
units.literal: Xian memorialized again, and he was banished to Hainan.

units.zh: 憲誅，召還。
units.en: After Yang Xian was executed, Guangyang was recalled.
units.literal: When Xian was executed, Guangyang was summoned back.

units.zh: 其冬，封忠勤伯，食祿三百六十石。
units.en: That winter he was made Baron of Loyal Diligence with three hundred sixty piculs.
units.literal: That winter he was enfeoffed Baron of Loyal Diligence with a stipend of three hundred sixty piculs.

units.zh: 誥詞稱其剸繁治劇，屢獻忠謀，比之子房、孔明。
units.en: His patent praised him for mastering tangled affairs and urgent business, for loyal counsel offered again and again, and likened him to Zifang and Zhuge Liang.
units.literal: The patent of enfeoffment praised him for cutting through complexity and managing urgent affairs, repeatedly offering loyal counsel, comparing him to Zifang and Kongming.

units.zh: 及善長以病去位，遂以廣洋為右丞相，參政胡惟庸為左丞。
units.en: When Shanzhang retired ill, Guangyang became Right Chancellor and Hu Weiyong Left Vice Director.
units.literal: When Shanzhang left office on grounds of illness, Guangyang was made Right Chancellor and Vice Commissioner Hu Weiyong Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 廣洋無所建白，久之，左遷廣東行省參政，而帝心終善廣洋，復召為左御史大夫。
units.en: He put forward little policy; eventually he was demoted to Guangdong, yet the Emperor still thought well of him and recalled him as Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Guangyang offered no proposals; after a long while he was demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Branch Secretariat, yet the Emperor's mind still favored Guangyang and he was again summoned as Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 十年復拜右丞相。
units.en: In year ten he was again named Right Chancellor.
units.literal: In the tenth year he was again appointed Right Chancellor.

units.zh: 廣洋頗耽酒，與惟庸同相，浮沉守位而已。
units.en: He drank heavily; sharing power with Hu Weiyong, he merely floated along in office.
units.literal: Guangyang was much given to wine; sharing the chancellorship with Hu Weiyong, he merely drifted and held his post.

units.zh: 帝數誡諭之。
units.en: The Emperor admonished him repeatedly.
units.literal: The Emperor several times admonished and instructed him.

units.zh: 十二年十二月，中丞塗節言劉基為惟庸毒死，廣洋宜知狀。
units.en: In the twelfth month of year twelve, Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Jie reported that Liu Ji had been poisoned by Hu Weiyong and that Guangyang should have known.
units.literal: In the twelfth year, twelfth month, Vice Censor-in-Chief Tu Jie said Liu Ji had been poisoned to death by Hu Weiyong; Guangyang ought to have known the circumstances.

units.zh: 帝問之，對曰：「無有。」
units.en: Questioned by the Emperor, he answered, "There was none."
units.literal: The Emperor questioned him; he replied: "There was none."

units.zh: 帝怒，責廣洋朋欺，貶廣南。
units.en: The Emperor raged, charged him with collusive deceit, and banished him to Guangnan.
units.literal: The Emperor was angry, rebuked Guangyang for factional deceit, and demoted him to Guangnan.

units.zh: 舟次太平，帝追怒其在江西曲庇文正，在中書不發楊憲奸，賜敕誅之。
units.en: At Taiping the Emperor's anger flared anew over his shielding of Wen Zheng in Jiangxi and his failure to expose Yang Xian at the Secretariat, and an edict ordered his death.
units.literal: When his boat reached Taiping, the Emperor in renewed anger that in Jiangxi he had bent the law to shield Wen Zheng and at the Secretariat had not exposed Yang Xian's treachery granted an edict ordering his execution.

units.zh: 廣洋少師余闕，淹通經史，善篆隸，工為歌詩。
units.en: As a youth he studied under Yu Que, mastered the classics and histories, excelled in seal and clerical script, and wrote verse with skill.
units.literal: In youth Guangyang studied under Yu Que, was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories, skilled in seal and clerical script, and adept at composing songs and poems.

units.zh: 為人寬和自守，與奸人同位而不能去，故及於禍。
units.en: Mild and self-restrained by nature, he sat beside wicked colleagues yet could not break away, and so came to ruin.
units.literal: As a man he was mild and guarded himself; sharing office with wicked men yet unable to remove himself, he therefore met disaster.

units.zh: 贊曰：明初設中書省，置左右丞相，管領樞要，率以勳臣領其事。
units.en: The appraisal runs: Early Ming established the Secretariat with left and right chancellors to govern the state's core, usually men of founding merit.
units.literal: The commentator says: At the beginning of Ming the Secretariat was established, with Left and Right Chancellors set to manage pivotal affairs, generally led by meritorious ministers.

units.zh: 然徐達、李文忠等數受命征討，未嘗專理省事。
units.en: Yet Xu Da, Li Wenzhong, and others were repeatedly sent on campaign and never devoted themselves solely to the Secretariat.
units.literal: Yet Xu Da, Li Wenzhong, and others several times received orders to campaign and never solely managed Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 其從容丞弼之任者，李善長、汪廣洋、胡惟庸三人而已。
units.en: Only Li Shanzhang, Wang Guangyang, and Hu Weiyong truly bore the steady work of assisting rule.
units.literal: Those who calmly assisted and supported were only Li Shanzhang, Wang Guangyang, and Hu Weiyong—three men alone.

units.zh: 惟庸敗後，丞相之官遂廢不設。
units.en: After Hu Weiyong's fall the chancellorship was abolished for good.
units.literal: After Hu Weiyong's fall the office of chancellor was then abolished and not re-established.

units.zh: 故終明之世，惟善長、廣洋得稱丞相。
units.en: Thus through the entire Ming only Shanzhang and Guangyang ever bore the title chancellor.
units.literal: Therefore through the whole Ming age only Shanzhang and Guangyang were called chancellor.

units.zh: 獨惜善長以布衣徒步，能擇主於草昧之初，委身戮力，贊成鴻業，遂得剖符開國，列爵上公，乃至富極貴溢，於衰暮之年自取覆滅。
units.en: It is a pity that Shanzhang, a man in plain sandals who chose his lord in the chaos of founding, gave his life to the cause, helped build the dynasty, won investiture and the highest rank, and stood at the summit of wealth—yet in old age destroyed himself.
units.literal: It is only to be regretted that Shanzhang, from common cloth on foot, could choose his lord at the dawn of the enterprise, devote his person and exhaust his strength, help accomplish the great achievement, and thereby obtain investiture and open a state, rank among upper dukes, even to the point that wealth and honor overflowed—yet in his declining years he brought ruin on himself.

units.zh: 廣洋謹厚自守，亦不能發奸遠禍。
units.en: Guangyang was cautious and upright, yet he could neither unmask traitors nor keep calamity at bay.
units.literal: Guangyang was prudent and thick in self-restraint, yet he too could not expose treachery and keep disaster far off.

units.zh: 俱致重譴，不亦大負爰立之初心，而有愧置諸左右之職業也夫？
units.en: Both suffered severe punishment—did they not grossly betray the trust placed in them at the throne's right hand?
units.literal: Both incurred heavy punishment—is this not a great betrayal of the original purpose in raising them up, and a shame to the profession of placing them at the left and right hand?
